topics.topic: Binding the pre-export checked project set to the later import selection
questions: When does the selected subset become fixed, and what prevents the owner from selecting at import a project whose room names were not checked before export?
How is the subset checked before export bound to the subset the owner later picks at import, given that the import accepts any subset and refuses no name?
How is the set of projects whose room names the owner checked bound to the subset later picked at import, given that R0-79 allows any subset and the import records or validates no such check?

quotes:
The only source is the Registry on the VPS, imported once. At the import the
owner picks any subset of its projects; the import accepts whatever the owner
picks then, and the choice recorded here binds nothing.

So the owner, before making the export on the VPS (R0-72), corrects
there every room name of the projects to be picked that breaks this rule
(owner, 2026-11-23, State 0 round-59 T1). The import then copies names the
owner has already checked; it writes no name of its own and refuses none.
judgement.why: The texts deliberately impose a procedural obligation on the owner while leaving Registry's import free to accept whatever subset the owner picks, with no recorded or enforced checked-project allowlist.

topics.topic: Definition and failure behavior of the source-side room-name correction action
questions: What concrete source-side action performs this correction, what inputs does it take, what observable success output does it produce, and how does it fail without leaving a partial or corrupt migration source?
What concrete source-side action lets the owner find and correct a room name on the VPS, and what are its input, authorization, output and failure result?
What must happen when a violating name cannot be corrected or the correction process is incomplete?
What concrete action lets the owner read and change a room name on the VPS, what observable result confirms it, and what happens if the correction cannot be applied?

quotes:
The owner makes the export of a source with a one-time migration script run on
that source's host. The script is not a Registry operation: production Registry
gains no export action, and the source keeps none after the migration. What
Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States
5 and 6.

So the owner, before making the export on the VPS (R0-72), corrects
there every room name of the projects to be picked that breaks this rule
(owner, 2026-11-23, State 0 round-59 T1). The import then copies names the
owner has already checked; it writes no name of its own and refuses none.
judgement.why: The concrete source-side correction procedure, its confirmation and its handling of incomplete correction are operational notes for the external migration preparation, not a Registry product action.

topics.topic: Preventing or detecting source changes between room-name checking and export
questions: How is it guaranteed that the names exported are the exact names the owner checked, if a room can be added or source data can change after the check and before the export is captured?
What prevents a room from being added or otherwise changed after the owner's check but before the export snapshot is made?
What prevents a room from being added or otherwise changed after the owner's check but before the export snapshot is made, and how is failure of that condition detected?

The owner makes the export of a source with a one-time migration script run on
that source's host. The script is not a Registry operation: production Registry
gains no export action, and the source keeps none after the migration. What
Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States
5 and 6.
judgement.why: Quiescing the legacy source, checking the completed export or detecting intervening changes concerns the operational ordering of the external check-and-export procedure and belongs to State 7 notes.

topics.topic: Whether pre-export room-name correction is an exception to room-name immutability
questions: Is the pre-export correction an explicit one-time exception to room-name immutability, or must non-compliant rooms be handled without renaming them?
Is the pre-export correction an explicit exception to R0-10, or must it occur without renaming the existing room?
How can the owner correct a room name when R0-10 requires that a room is never renamed or removed; is this a one-time exception for the v1 source, or must the migration use another remedy?

quotes:
A room is created in a project and listed; it is never renamed or removed.
Nothing more is added until a consumer needs it.

The import
renames no room: it stores a picked project's rooms under the names the v1
instance gave them (A16), and a room is never renamed or removed afterwards
(R0-10). So the owner, before making the export on the VPS (R0-72), corrects
there every room name of the projects to be picked that breaks this rule
(owner, 2026-11-23, State 0 round-59 T1).

Legacy instances — the v1 Registries running before production: the one
  on the VPS, inside Client Portal's network, and the local one. They hold real
  personal data, are administered by the owner and stand outside this
  document's guarantees. The VPS one is the migration's only source; each is
  retired once the migration is done (R0-79).
judgement.why: The correction occurs in the legacy VPS instance before import, which stands outside these guarantees, while R0-10 governs the imported Registry room afterwards, so the obligations do not apply incompatibly to the same record history.

topics.topic: Whether archived source projects may be modified for migration
questions: May the owner correct room names in an archived source project before export, and if so is this a migration-only exception to archive finality?
May the owner correct a room name in an archived source project before export, and if so, what exact exception overrides R0-12?

quotes:
An archived project never returns to `active` and cannot be corrected.
Archiving it again returns it unchanged — its updated time does not move.

Legacy instances — the v1 Registries running before production: the one
  on the VPS, inside Client Portal's network, and the local one. They hold real
  personal data, are administered by the owner and stand outside this
  document's guarantees. The VPS one is the migration's only source; each is
  retired once the migration is done (R0-79).

So the owner, before making the export on the VPS (R0-72), corrects
there every room name of the projects to be picked that breaks this rule
(owner, 2026-11-23, State 0 round-59 T1). The import then copies names the
owner has already checked; it writes no name of its own and refuses none.
judgement.why: R0-12 governs correction of projects in the specified Registry, whereas the required room-name preparation occurs on the legacy VPS instance that expressly stands outside the document's guarantees, including when the picked source project is archived.

topics.topic: Evidence and responsibility for verifying every copied room name was checked
questions: What fact or observable result establishes that every copied room name was checked, and who records or verifies it?

topics.topic: Exact source value used as an imported v1 room name and handling invalid values
questions: What exact source value is copied as a room's name when A16 is not supplied here: the stored value verbatim, a derived display value, or a normalized/defaulted value, and what happens when that value is absent or invalid?

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
